summary: Lake County, MT lookout: 1916 two-story log house, 1934 L-4 tower, 1959-60 R-6 tower; staffed through 1972, removed by 1979. Sources disagree on 1959 vs 1960.

facts.design: 53-foot treated timber R-6 tower, last of three structures (two-story log house, 50-foot L-4 tower)
facts.status_note: Removed by 1979, per FireLookout.com; no source describes what remains at the site.

events.note: Two-story log house with a hip roof
Forest Service photograph captioned Jim Creek lookout, 1923; same style as the original Spotted Bear lookout of 1914
Log house replaced by a 50-foot L-4 tower
Packer carried lookout supplies to the station (Flathead Courier, June 30, 1949)
Forest Service staff building a new lookout in October 1959; workers left their posts when high winds hit in November 1959
53-foot treated timber R-6 tower, a quarter of the way up the sidehill (FireLookout.com date; 1959 newspaper notes show work under way)
Listed among 21 lookouts occupied on the Flathead National Forest during the fire season

evidence.supports: built in 1916 as a two-story log house with a hip roof; replaced in 1934 by a 50-foot L-4 tower
evidence.quote: Built in 1916, this 2-story log house with hip roof was replaced in 1934 by a 50' L-4 tower.

evidence.supports: 1960 53-foot treated timber R-6 tower a quarter of the way up the sidehill
evidence.quote: In 1960, a 53' treated timber R-6 tower was constructed 1/4 of the way up the sidehill.
The lookout was staffed through 1972 and removed by 1979.

evidence.supports: location 16 miles southeast of Polson in Lake County
1957 and 1958 lookout personnel listed as couples
evidence.quote: Known lookout personnel: 1957: Mr. & Mrs. John Bergmann; 1958: Mr. & Mrs. Allan Howsmon.

evidence.supports: 1949 packer took lookout supplies to the station
evidence.quote: Gene Fox, packer at Condon, took the lookout supplies to Jim Creek lookout station, Monday.

evidence.supports: October 1959 Forest Service personnel staying at the lookout while building a new one
evidence.quote: Several Forest Service personnel are staying at Jim Creek lookout where they are building a new lookout.

evidence.supports: November 1959 workers left their posts when high winds hit
evidence.quote: Herb Styler, Art and Robert Anderson, who have been stationed on Jim Lookout working on construction of the new tower, gave up their posts Wednesday when the high winds hit.

evidence.supports: listed as gone, Flathead National Forest, Lake County
1923 photograph captioned as the Jim Creek lookout
1923 lookout identical in style to the original Spotted Bear lookout built in 1914
evidence.quote: This lookout was identical in style to the original Spotted Bear lookout, built in 1914

evidence.supports: four lookouts occupied by women during World War II, including Jim Creek
evidence.quote: The Flathead had four lookouts occupied by women then: Nine Mile, Mission, Crane Mountain, and Jim Creek.

evidence.supports: 1966 list of occupied lookouts includes Jim Creek
evidence.quote: McCaffery, Mission, Cooney, Jim Creek, Elbow, Desert, Baptiste

sources.title: Trails of the Past: Historical Overview of the Flathead National Forest, Montana, 1800-1960

corrections.why: The two-story log house stood only from 1916 until it was replaced in 1934 by an L-4 tower; a tower stood on the site until it was removed by 1979. The FFLA list still labels it 2-Story cab, so the editor should decide.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FireLookout.com dates the 53-foot R-6 tower to 1960. Forest Lookouts quotes Flathead Courier notes from October and November 1959 describing work on the new tower. The story reports both and does not choose one.

notes_for_editor: Core dates come from FireLookout.com, with newspaper notes and a Forest Service history for staffing and the 1923 photo. The FireLookout.com page title and search snippet call this a 'Fire Lookout Cabin' offering accommodations, but the page text I read (R.I.P. 1916-1934, no rental mention) does not say that; check for a rental before setting any rental or access field. The 1923 photo is a Forest Service figure with no direct image URL, so no photo entry was added.
